children: The National Bank of Morocco left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 2.25% at its September 2026 meeting, marking a sixth consecutive hold and keeping borrowing costs at their lowest level since 2022.
Policymakers stated that the impact of elevated energy prices remained limited, mitigated by subsidies on road transport and the continued maintenance of gas and electricity prices.
As food prices declined, inflation remained low, averaging 0.3% during the first eight months of the year.
Agricultural output is expected to rebound by 16% in 2026, while non-agricultural activity is forecast to slow to 3.1%.

Looking ahead, inflation is expected to average 0.7% in 2026 before rising to 1.5% in 2027, driven by an acceleration in core inflation to 2.2% as the contraction in food prices is offset by higher imported inflation.
Economic growth is expected to slow to 4.4% in 2026 and 2.9% in 2027, amid a projected 7.6% contraction in agricultural output.

title: Morocco Maintains Policy Rate at 2.25%
